 Three Social Security payments in 7 days starting October 28: Why November SSI arrives early and the full payout schedule
 SECTIONS Three Social Security payments in 7 days starting October 28: Why November SSI arrives early and the full payout schedule By Mukesh Thapliyal , Global Desk Last Updated: Oct 26, 2026, 01:24:00 PM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis For Social Security recipients, three key payment dates are coming up from October 28 to November 3. The initial payment on October 28 caters to those with birthdays from the 21st to the 31st. Following that, on October 30, an early deposit for Supplemental Security Income will be issued since November 1 lands on a Sunday.
 Reuters The early arrival does not increase anyone’s entitlement.
 Three federal benefit payment dates fall within seven days beginning October 28, but that does not mean every Social Security recipient will receive three checks. The schedule brings together October’s final birthday-based payment, an early November Supplemental Security Income (SSI) deposit and November’s payment for certain longtime beneficiaries. For households planning rent, groceries and utility bills, the distinction matters. There is also an important change in November’s calendar: one payment arrives November 10, rather than November 11, because of Veterans Day , which is a federal holiday.
 WHO GETS PAID BETWEEN OCTOBER 28 AND NOVEMBER 3?
 According to Futbolete, the October 28 payment closes the month’s regular Social Security cycle for beneficiaries whose qualifying birthdays fall between the 21st and 31st. That includes eligible retirement, survivor and disability beneficiaries following the Wednesday schedule.
Next comes SSI on Friday, October 30. November 1 falls on a Sunday, so November’s payment moves to the preceding business day. Recipients who received their October SSI payment on October 1 will therefore see another deposit before the month ends.

 The early arrival does not increase anyone’s entitlement. October 30 delivers November’s SSI benefit, so there is no separate SSI payment scheduled during November.
 The third date is Tuesday, November 3. The Social Security Administration ’s calendar assigns that payment to people who received Social Security before May 1997 and those receiving both Social Security and SSI.
Together, October 28, October 30 and November 3 span seven calendar days, counting both endpoints. They cover different recipient groups. Someone receiving both programs may get SSI on October 30 and Social Security on November 3, rather than all three payments.

 NOVEMBER’S FULL PAYMENT SCHEDULE
 The official SSA calendar confirms the following dates for November benefits: 
 October 30: November SSI arrives early because November 1 is Sunday.
 November 3: Social Security for beneficiaries covered by the pre-May 1997 or dual-benefit payment rules.
 November 10: Benefits for the birthday group covering the 1st through the 10th. The usual second-Wednesday payment shifts forward because November 11 is Veterans Day.
 November 18 (Third Wednesday): Benefits for the birthday group covering the 11th through the 20th.
 November 25 (Fourth Wednesday): Benefits for the birthday group covering the 21st through the 31st.
 For spouses receiving benefits through a partner’s work record, Futbolete notes that the relevant birthday belongs to the worker whose record supports the benefit and not by the spouse’s. Checking that detail can prevent confusion when matching a household’s payment to the calendar.
